name: Chordoid Glioma of the Third Ventricle
aliases: Chordoid Glioma of the Third Ventricle

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Chordoid Glioma

criteria.description: Tumor located in the anterior third ventricle region
Histological features showing chordoid appearance with epithelioid cells in mucinous stroma
Positive immunostaining for GFAP and vimentin with EMA negativity
Symptoms consistent with third ventricular mass effect such as headache and visual disturbances

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of tumor in anterior third ventricle with characteristic histopathological features and immunohistochemical profile
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Definitive diagnosis requires histopathological confirmation after surgical biopsy or resection.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Obstructive hydrocephalus due to third ventricle mass effect
Progressive headache associated with increased intracranial pressure
Visual field defects secondary to optic chiasm compression
searchTerms: visual field loss from optic nerve pressure
blind spots due to optic chiasm compression

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting related to raised intracranial pressure
searchTerms: nausea and vomiting from brain pressure
vomiting related to increased head pressure
feeling sick due to raised intracranial pressure

occasional.symptomName: Diplopia due to cranial nerve involvement

laboratory: CSF analysis typically normal or nonspecific
Endocrine hormone panel may show hypothalamic-pituitary axis abnormalities
imaging: MRI showing well-circumscribed, homogeneously enhancing mass in anterior third ventricle
T2-weighted MRI hyperintensity with minimal surrounding edema
genetic: No recurrent genetic mutations identified; molecular profile not well established
other: Histopathology reveals chordoid morphology with epithelioid cells in mucinous stroma
Immunohistochemistry positive for GFAP and vimentin, negative for EMA

distinguishingFeatures: Ependymomas typically arise from ventricular lining with perivascular pseudorosettes
Immunohistochemistry positive for EMA and variable GFAP
Chordomas arise from notochordal remnants, usually at clivus or sacrum
Histology shows physaliphorous cells with abundant vacuolated cytoplasm
Meningiomas show dural attachment and whorled cell patterns
Positive for EMA and progesterone receptor

redFlags: Signs of acute hydrocephalus such as sudden headache and vomiting
Visual loss or severe visual field defects
references: Brat DJ, Scheithauer BW, Fuller GN, et al. Chordoid glioma of the third ventricle: a distinctive tumor with unique clinical and pathologic features. Am J Surg Pathol. 1998;22(9):1030-1038.
